title: Naturality of normalized completed integral scalar maps
statement: Let ell be prime, E/Q_ell a finite normed field extension, and h:T→U a scheme morphism. Suppose T,U are Noetherian and finite dimensional, ell is invertible in every local ring, and s_T,s_U are any normalized scalar realization data of [lem-weil-pbc-realization-scalar-functor]. Write a_W=s_W.integralIso followed by s_W.inclusion. Let c_A:h^{-1}A_U→A_T be the canonical completed finite-coefficient comparison of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and c_E:h^{-1}E_U→E_T the continuous precomposition map. Then c_A followed by a_T equals h^{-1}(a_U) followed by c_E. The scalar maps are precisely the specified normalized presentations; no arbitrary coefficient identification is substituted.

proof.text:
a finite coefficient comparison is uniquely determined by its values on
constant sections, since those sections generate the constant sheaf locally.
The finite normalization of sT and sU therefore identifies their comparisons
with the canonical discrete-function comparisons. Their pullback squares commute
on constants, hence on all sections. The completed comparison is determined by
its finite projections: integral_normalization says that those are pointwise
reduction. Separatedness of the complete valuation ring then gives the integral
pullback square. Finally inclusion_normalization uniquely identifies each
inclusion with pointwise inclusion into E. Continuous precomposition commutes
with this inclusion, proving the displayed scalar square. Empty test objects
cause no exception, since equality of their sections is automatic.
